explanations: terra: فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ likewise joins following to guidance and promises the followers freedom from fear and grief.

luna: The section’s preference root ء ث ر names choosing one thing ahead of another; this ayah says people “bought the life of this world for the Hereafter” (ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ), spelling out the cost of the wrong order. | terra: ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ treats the wrong ordering as an exchange of the later life for the near one.
terra: Whatever good people send forward for themselves they will find with God, making present action an advance deposit at the later destination.
terra: The change of direction reveals who follows the Messenger and who turns back on his heels, a precise leader-and-follower test with reversal built into the bodily image.

luna: The section’s dictionary wording السَّابِقُ الأَوَّل evokes precedence; this ayah uses فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ, “race toward good things,” making that precedence an active pursuit of good. | terra: فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ makes differing directions converge in a race for good, giving the running image its proper object.
terra: God desires ease for people and does not desire hardship, stating the moral polarity behind being eased toward the easy course.

luna: This ayah describes one group asking only for worldly good and having no share in the Hereafter; 2:201 supplies the contrasting prayer for good in both lives, so this row gives the section’s wrong ordering a precise example. | terra: One class asks only for a worldly share and consequently has no share in the hereafter, making exclusive desire for the first stage determine the loss of the later one.

luna: In contrast to the world-only request of 2:200, this ayah asks for good in this world and the Hereafter and protection from the Fire, showing a rightly ordered desire that does not discard either life. | terra: The next class asks for good in both the world and the hereafter, establishing a boundary against reading the section's comparison as abandonment of every worldly good.

luna: After the two prayers contrasted in 2:200–201, this ayah says each group has a share from what it earned; its contribution is to attach the final allotment to deeds rather than to the first request alone.
terra: The near life is adorned for rejecters who mock believers, but the God-conscious will be above them on resurrection day; the final height reverses the visible worldly rank.
terra: Guard all prayers and ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ; one prayer is explicitly located within an ordered series, echoing the positional sense developed for the prayer root.

luna: The section’s image uses a horse train to make worldly preference visible; this ayah lists branded horses among the attractions of worldly life, then contrasts that adornment with the better return with God. | terra: Branded horses are among the beautified desires of ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا, while the good return is with God; the horse image itself becomes part of the near-life test.

luna: After 3:14 lists horses and other worldly attractions, this ayah asks whether the audience should be told of what is better and names Gardens and God’s pleasure; its own contribution is the superior return beyond the attractions in its neighbour.

terra: مَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ gives a concrete act of storing for later, plausibly echoing the source dictionary's horse that holds some running in reserve, though the objects and scene differ.
luna: This ayah likewise says the righteous “hasten in good deeds” (يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ); it is another concrete Qur’anic use of speed to reach good rather than favor the immediate life.

luna: Like the section’s reordering of what is worth reaching first, this ayah commands, “Race toward forgiveness” (وَسَارِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ) and a Garden from the Lord. | terra: وَسَارِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ directs speed toward forgiveness and the garden, a nonlexical race toward the enduring prize.

luna: The section weighs preference for the near life against the later one; this ayah says the person seeking worldly reward receives from it, while the person seeking the Hereafter’s reward receives from it, after first setting each life within an appointed term of death.
terra: مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ divides one battle line by the two different goals its members put first.

luna: The section says the first arrival does not decide the winner; this ayah defines the one who truly succeeds as whoever is moved away from the Fire and admitted to the Garden (فَقَدْ فَازَ), so success is judged at the later outcome.

luna: The section says the later life is better and more lasting; this ayah calls the worldly enjoyment little and the Hereafter better for the God-fearing, directly adding duration and value to the comparison. | terra: مَتَـٰعُ ٱلدُّنْيَا قَلِيلٌ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ makes the near stage brief and the later stage better.

luna: The section says the dictionary sense of ص ل و can name the second horse following the first but keeps the Qur’anic prayer sense; here prayer groups alternate, and the group that has prostrated is put behind the one still serving, uniting prayer with succession. | terra: The danger-prayer instructions place one troop in prayer with the Prophet, then bring forward another troop that has not yet prayed; صَلَاة is enacted as ordered companies following their leader.

luna: The section warns against preferring the nearer life over what lasts; this ayah supplies a boundary by saying that with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter, so the choice of reward is not limited to the first life. | terra: Whoever wants worldly reward is reminded that both worldly and later reward are with God, relocating control of both stages from the chooser to their Lord.
terra: وَقَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم بِعِيسَى places Jesus after earlier prophets on their traces, a historical relay of leader and follower.

luna: This ayah repeats فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ, a race toward good, then says all return to God; it joins the section’s race order to its later destination. | terra: فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ again turns human difference into a race whose result is finally disclosed by God.

luna: The section says the Hereafter is better than the near life; this ayah calls worldly life play and amusement and says the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing (خَيْرٌ), a direct restatement in other words. | terra: Worldly life is play and distraction, while وَلَلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ for the God-conscious; it restates which stage is truly better.
terra: فَبِهُدَىٰهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ commands following the guidance of earlier prophets, joining direction with taking predecessors as one's lead.

luna: The section’s ordered course is not simply a contest of speed; this ayah says no community can hasten or delay its appointed term (لَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ سَاعَةً وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ), bounding the image with a fixed end. | terra: At an appointed term, a community can neither يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ nor يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ even an hour; temporal position is pictured as lagging or advancing.
terra: As communities enter the Fire in succession, أُخْرَىٰهُمْ addresses أُولَىٰهُمْ; rear and front groups meet at the wrong finish.
terra: أُولَىٰهُمْ answers أُخْرَىٰهُمْ, completing the exchange between the first and last groups in 7:38.
luna: The section says preferring worldly life leaves the later life behind; this ayah describes people deceived by worldly life who forget the meeting of that Day, a concrete form of that neglect.
terra: A corrupt succession takes عَرَضَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ, while وَٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ; “the nearer/lower” makes the spatial root of worldly preference audible.

luna: The section explicitly gives the dictionary pair العُدْوَةُ الدُّنْيَا / العُدْوَةُ القُصْوَى, near and far bank; this ayah stages the two forces on those two banks, showing how الدُّنْيَا names spatial nearness as well as the near life. | terra: ٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا and ٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ are the literal near and far banks named by the source section, spatializing its two temporal destinations.

luna: The section’s root ء ث ر names preferring, and its scene is a course; this ayah commands setting out, then describes people clinging to earth and preferring the worldly life to the Hereafter (ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ), a refusal to enter the course toward the lasting good. | terra: The question أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ rebukes settling for the near life when its enjoyment is tiny beside the later one.

luna: The section’s dictionary phrase السَّابِقُ الأَوَّل pairs being first with being ahead; this ayah praises the first forerunners and those who follow them in goodness, a boundary showing that precedence can be honored when it is faithfulness rather than preference for worldly life. | terra: ٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ are the foremost first ones, followed by وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُم; the race's leaders and the train behind them appear together.

luna: The section warns of choosing the near life and neglecting the later one; this ayah describes people content with worldly life and heedless of God’s signs, with an adverse abode as their outcome. | terra: Those who do not expect the meeting with God رَضُوا۟ بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱطْمَأَنُّوا۟ بِهَا, concretely describing satisfaction with the first stage.
terra: When the appointed time arrives, people cannot fall behind or get ahead by an hour, a fixed finish no runner can alter.

luna: This ayah describes people who want the life of this world and its adornment; 11:16 states the consequence as having no share in the Hereafter, so this row supplies the preference the image criticizes. | terra: Whoever wants the worldly life and its adornment can be paid there in full, establishing the apparently successful early leg of the course.

luna: After 11:15’s worldly-life pursuit, this ayah says such people will have nothing in the Hereafter (لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ إِلَّا ٱلنَّارُ), a stark reversal of the lasting reward in the section. | terra: For the people of 11:15 there is only fire in the hereafter, revealing why full payment at the first stage was not victory.

luna: The section’s root ب ق ي names what remains and lasts; in a warning against dishonest trade this ayah says what remains from God is better (بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ), making the lasting remainder preferable to immediate gain. | terra: بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ says that God's remainder is better than fraudulent gain, joining “remaining” and “better” in a concrete commercial choice.
terra: Prayer is established at the day's two ends and near portions of night, placing صَلَوٰة at successive positions on a temporal line.
terra: Joseph's brothers say إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ, an explicit human race whose reported sequence drives the scene.
terra: وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ stages two people racing for the same door with opposed aims, showing that shared speed need not mean a shared moral course.
terra: Joseph orders that most of the early harvest be left in its ears, a concrete strategy of withholding present capacity for the later part of the course.
terra: The hard years consume what was قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ except a guarded remainder, showing why spending the whole reserve at the beginning would fail.
terra: Joseph's brothers confess that God preferred him over them; the preference root returns within the story whose brothers earlier said they had gone racing in 12:17.
luna: The section pictures runners with an ordered course; this ayah says the sun and moon each run to an appointed term, making their motion bounded by an endpoint.

luna: The section condemns preferring the near life; this ayah says people rejoice in worldly life while its enjoyment is small beside the Hereafter, giving that preference a specific short-lived object. | terra: وَمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَـٰعٌ reduces the near life's apparent lead to a temporary provision when viewed from the later stage.
terra: ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ precisely states the wrong preference between the two positions.
terra: مَّا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ makes a community unable either to outrun its term or trail it.

luna: The section orders a procession from front to rear; this ayah says God knows those who come forward and those who remain behind (ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ ... ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ). Its referents are disputed, so it supplies a positional parallel without identifying them as racers. | terra: God knows ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ and ٱلْمُسْتَـْٔخِرِينَ, the ones advanced and the ones remaining behind in the human sequence.
terra: When the appointed term comes, people cannot move it backward or forward, applying the section's positional vocabulary to time.

luna: The section’s root ب ق ي evokes the horse that keeps part of its run in reserve; this ayah contrasts what is with people and runs out with what is with God and remains (وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ), making endurance explicit. | terra: مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ gives the section's endurance claim as a direct contrast between exhaustion and remaining.
terra: ٱسْتَحَبُّوا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ again identifies love of the nearer stage over the later one as the decisive error.

luna: The section’s image warns that preferring what is near misorders the outcome; this ayah describes one who wants the immediate life and hastens for it, then names Hell as the end, so speed toward the first reward is not the final win. | terra: Whoever wants ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ may receive an accelerated share before being assigned Hell; immediate arrival is explicitly detached from final success.

luna: Against the section’s near-life preference, this ayah describes one who wills the Hereafter and strives for it as a believer; its acknowledged effort makes the later destination a course to pursue. | terra: Whoever wants the hereafter and سَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا directs striving toward its proper later goal.

terra: Between the immediate seeker of 17:18 and the higher final ranks of 17:21, this ayah says both groups receive an extension of the Lord's gift, distinguishing present provision from final placement.

luna: The section says the first arrival is not the winner and the Hereafter is better; this ayah explicitly says the Hereafter is greater in degrees and preference (أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَٰتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا), measuring rank beyond this life. | terra: The hereafter has أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَـٰتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا; after 17:18-19's two courses, the final ranking exceeds the preliminary one.
terra: Prayer runs from the sun's decline through nightfall to dawn recitation, again distributing worship across an ordered daily course.
terra: The Prophet may consume himself عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم after people turn away, preserving the image of someone left behind at the tracks of those departing.
terra: The Prophet is told not to turn his eyes from those calling on their Lord in desire for زِينَةَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا, a concrete boundary on near-life preference.
terra: Rain-fed worldly growth becomes dry fragments scattered by wind, providing the vanishing foreground against which 18:46 names the remaining good deeds.

luna: The section’s root ب ق ي names what lasts; this ayah contrasts the worldly life’s adornment with “the abiding good deeds” (وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ), which are better in reward and hope. | terra: ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ are better with the Lord than wealth and children, making the enduring entrant outrank the near life's adornments.
luna: The section’s runners are measured by where they finally arrive; this ayah depicts all people presented before their Lord “in a row” (صَفًّا), transferring the line image to judgment.

luna: The section’s dictionary form أثر is another’s trail; Moses and his companion retrace their tracks (عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا), a concrete reversal of forward running that shows the same following relation can turn back. | terra: Moses and his servant turn back عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا, literally following their own tracks in reverse.
terra: Guidance increases for the guided, and ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ are better in reward and return; it joins guidance, remaining, and the better destination.
terra: أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِى directly joins prayer to remembrance, preserving the worship sense while the section hears a second horse behind it.
terra: Pharaoh's magicians ask to be أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ; the contest makes being first a deliberate tactic that does not win the encounter.
terra: Moses is told to cast what is in his hand and it swallows their craft, supplying the result that overturns the first move of 20:65.
terra: Pharaoh boasts that his punishment is أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ; 20:73 answers the counterfeit claim to endurance with وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ.
terra: The magicians answer لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ and limit Pharaoh's power to هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا, reversing the choice made in 87:16.

luna: The section’s wording “better and longer-lasting” is echoed by the believers’ declaration “God is better and more lasting” (وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ), choosing God’s reward over Pharaoh’s threat. | terra: وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ supplies 20:72's reason and closely matches the claim that the later good is better and more enduring.
terra: Moses leads a moving company on a dry path through the sea and is told not to fear دَرَكًا, being caught from behind; water, a track, and pursuit converge.
terra: Pharaoh follows the departing company with his forces and the sea covers them, completing 20:77's front-and-rear pursuit.
terra: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُۥ وَمَا هَدَىٰ names the man at the head as a false guide, the reversal of a leading front that truly directs its followers.

luna: The section’s dictionary form أثر means coming on another’s trace; Moses says his people are “right behind me” (عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى) while he has hurried ahead, a literal following order like the second horse behind the leader. | terra: Moses says his people are عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى and that he hurried ahead; this exactly stages a leader, followers on his trace, and unequal positions in one moving line.
terra: فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ makes safety depend on following divine guidance, aligning a follower behind the true guide.
terra: The command to glorify before sunrise, before sunset, through the night, and at the day's edges lays تَسْبِيح along a temporal course with successive positions.

luna: The section’s root ب ق ي evokes what endures; this ayah tells the Prophet not to covet worldly enjoyments and says the Lord’s provision is better and more lasting (خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ), closely matching the section’s valuation. | terra: The flower of ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا is set against وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ, joining the near attraction to what is better and longer-lasting.

luna: The section’s root س ب ح develops motion and glorification, and its horse image values endurance; this ayah says the angels glorify night and day without tiring. It offers a sustained-action parallel, though it does not depict a race.

luna: The section’s dictionary form سَبَحَ means swimming and its image gives it a moving course; this ayah says night, day, sun, and moon each “swim in an orbit” (كُلٌّ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ), extending the motion from a horse line to the heavens. | terra: The night, day, sun, and moon each فِى فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ, directly realizing the source dictionary's stars swimming in their orbit.
terra: God makes them leaders يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا, joining a place at the front with the act of guiding those behind.
terra: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ describes a household whose haste is in good works, not in seizing the near life.
terra: مَا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ repeats the boundary that no collective can overtake its measured term.

luna: The section turns life choice into a race; this ayah describes the God-fearing as “racing in good deeds” (يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ), giving the image a positive course. | terra: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَـٰبِقُونَ joins hastening in good works to being their forerunners.

luna: The section’s dictionary sense of س ب ح connects movement with the glorification commanded in 87:1, while 87:15 names prayer; this ayah brings the senses together in birds with wings spread, each knowing its prayer and praise. | terra: Birds in ranks each know صَلَاتَهُۥ وَتَسْبِيحَهُۥ; one ayah unites the two roots whose animal-motion senses build the section without replacing prayer or glorification.
terra: The servants of the Merciful يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا; their gentle gait is a nonlexical moral counterpart to the well-stepping animal in the source dictionary.
terra: Pharaoh's force pursues Moses' company at sunrise, clearly staging one moving group behind another.
terra: The two companies see one another and Moses' followers fear they will be caught, supplying the closing distance in the pursuit of 26:60.
terra: Moses answers that his Lord will guide him, identifying true guidance at the head of the pursued company.
terra: The sea is struck open into a dry route and each parted side rises like a mountain, giving the guided train of 26:60-62 its path through water.
terra: A man comes running from the farthest edge of the city, a second Qur'anic scene in which purposeful speed begins at the remote boundary.

luna: The section says the later life is better and lasts; this ayah says what is with God is better and more lasting (خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ) than worldly enjoyment and adornment. | terra: What people receive is worldly enjoyment and adornment, whereas مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ; the visible first portion is not the lasting winner.
terra: The one meeting a good promise is contrasted with one merely furnished with worldly enjoyment and then brought to judgment, extending 28:60's better-and-lasting comparison.
terra: To God belongs praise فِى ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ, spanning the first and later lives rather than treating the first as self-sufficient.
luna: The section condemns preferring worldly life to the later one; this ayah supplies a boundary on that choice: seek the Hereafter with what God gave, yet do not forget one’s share of this world.
terra: Those who want ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا envy Korah's visible splendor, staging the attraction of the nearer reward.
terra: Those given knowledge answer that ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ, correcting the spectators of 28:79 with the better later valuation.

luna: The section says that being first in the near life is not the win; this ayah reserves the Hereafter home for those who do not seek exaltation or corruption on earth, a direct boundary on striving for worldly precedence. | terra: The later abode is assigned to those who do not seek worldly elevation or corruption, reversing the assumption that being high in the first stage secures the last.
terra: Everything perishes except God's face, a direct formulation of what exhausts its course and what alone remains.

luna: The section says the later life outlasts the near one; this ayah calls the worldly life amusement and play but the Hereafter the true life (لَهِىَ ٱلْحَيَوَانُ), clarifying which stage endures. | terra: Worldly life is play and diversion, while the later abode is described as the true life; the contrast sharply separates apparent early animation from lasting life.
terra: Those who strive for God are promised لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا, joining sustained exertion to being directed onto the routes.
terra: فِىٓ أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ uses the same family for the nearest land, another literal spatial counterpart to “the near life.”

luna: The section’s temporal image opposes the near life to the later one; this ayah says people know the outward appearance of worldly life while heedless of the Hereafter, specifying the limited horizon of that choice. | terra: People know the outward surface of ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا while remaining heedless of the hereafter, mistaking the visible front of the sequence for the whole.
terra: وَٱقْصِدْ فِى مَشْيِكَ commands a measured gait, making bodily step and moral measure coincide as they do in the section's easy-moving animal.

luna: Like the section’s course that has a leading and trailing place, this ayah describes night entering day, then says the sun and moon each run to a fixed term; its own contribution is the measured celestial course.
terra: Leaders from among the people يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا through patience, another explicit meeting of leadership and guidance.
terra: The Prophet's wives are explicitly offered worldly life and its adornment as one possible choice.
terra: Against 33:28's worldly option, choosing God, His Messenger, and the later abode leads to the prepared great reward.
terra: The promised day cannot be delayed or advanced by an hour, fixing every entrant's place on the temporal course.
luna: This ayah repeats the sun and moon running to an appointed term; it extends the section’s image of motion that has a limited course and duration.
terra: Among the heirs of the Book is سَابِقٌۢ بِٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ, the one who goes ahead through good deeds rather than mere temporal priority.
terra: God records مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَـٰرَهُمْ, joining what people send ahead with the traces left behind them.
terra: A man comes مِنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ, running from the farthest edge toward the messengers' cause.
terra: ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مَن لَّا يَسْـَٔلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ turns 36:20's runner into one who calls his people to follow the rightly guided.

luna: The section’s dictionary form سَبَحَ is swimming and its race image gives it a running motion; this ayah says the sun cannot catch the moon, night does not precede day, and each “swims” in an orbit, making the ordered course itself the point rather than first arrival. | terra: The sun cannot overtake the moon, night is not a forerunner of day, and all يَسْبَحُونَ in an orbit; one ayah joins swimming, racing precedence, and a divinely fixed order.
terra: At the trumpet people rush from their graves toward their Lord, relocating the decisive mass movement to the later life.
terra: If God willed, people would race toward the path yet be unable to see it; speed without sight or guidance cannot secure the course.
luna: The section pictures a troop arranged in a running line; this surah opens by swearing by those “ranged in ranks” (وَٱلصَّٰٓفَّٰتِ صَفًّا), a direct formation parallel.

luna: The section’s dictionary form أثر is following someone’s track; this ayah says the heedless rush along their ancestors’ footsteps (عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ), turning a following line into a hurried inherited course. | terra: فَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ depicts people rushing in their predecessors' tracks, showing that energetic following can carry the train in the wrong direction.

luna: This ayah says each angel has a known station (مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ); 37:165 gives their own contribution as standing in ranks, so this row supplies the assigned positions behind the section’s ordered troop.
luna: The section’s line of first and following runners has a direct formation parallel in the angels’ “standing in ranks” (وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ).

luna: The section’s root س ب ح links movement to glorification; after the line of angels in 37:165, this ayah calls them those who glorify (ٱلْمُسَبِّحُونَ), joining ordered ranks to the root’s worship sense.
terra: ٱلصَّـٰفِنَـٰتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ are fine horses presented to Solomon, placing the section's animal image inside a test of attachment and remembrance.
terra: Solomon's حُبَّ ٱلْخَيْرِ and ذِكْرِ رَبِّى are held in a deliberately difficult relation as the horses disappear, illuminating the boundary between created attraction and remembrance.
terra: The returned horses' legs and أَعْنَاقِ are touched; their necks concretize the source dictionary's claim that a horse-train's guiding front can be its necks.
luna: The section’s image gives a runner a course and an end; this ayah says the sun and moon each run to a fixed term (كُلٌّ يَجْرِى لِأَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّى), joining motion to an appointed duration.
terra: ٱتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ explicitly aligns a follower behind a speaker who guides him on the sound road.

luna: The section says what follows is better and longer-lasting; this ayah calls the present life a temporary enjoyment and the Hereafter the abode of permanence (دَارُ ٱلْقَرَارِ), making duration the decisive difference. | terra: إِنَّمَا هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا مَتَـٰعٌ وَإِنَّ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ هِىَ دَارُ ٱلْقَرَارِ contrasts passing enjoyment with the settled abode.

luna: The section compares near and later life and says the later is better; this ayah makes the choice a cultivation whose harvest differs: the Hereafter’s yield is increased, while the worldly-life seeker receives only what is allotted here. | terra: The harvest of the hereafter grows, while one seeking the worldly harvest receives some of it and has no later share; two aims produce two finishes.

luna: The section’s wording “better and longer-lasting” is repeated here: the worldly provision is enjoyment, while what is with God is better and more enduring (خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ). | terra: Worldly provision is مَتَـٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا, while what is with God is خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ; this is the section's two-stage comparison almost verbatim.
terra: A people claim they are عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ; the ayah brings guidance and following traces together while exposing their mistaken equation.

luna: The section’s dictionary form أثر includes coming on someone’s trace; the deniers say they follow their fathers’ footsteps (عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ), showing the line of followers as inherited allegiance. | terra: The privileged repeat that they are عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ, making inherited tracks rather than truth determine who leads their line.
terra: Abraham leaves a كَلِمَةًۢ بَاقِيَةً فِى عَقِبِهِ, a word remaining among those behind him in the generational line.
terra: Worldly luxury is reduced to the enjoyment of the near life, while the hereafter with the Lord belongs to the God-conscious.

luna: The section affirms that the later life exists and lasts; this ayah gives the contrary claim, “there is only our worldly life” (مَا هِىَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنْيَا), and attributes death to time, a boundary that makes the section’s second stage contested.
terra: The rejecters argue that if revelation were good others would not have سَبَقُونَا إِلَيْهِ; their claim exposes the false assumption that social rank determines who may get ahead.
terra: What is earlier and what is later of the Prophet's burden are expressed with forms of advancing and delaying, turning temporal extent into front-and-back position.
terra: The command to glorify before sunrise and before sunset places praise at two ordered points of the daily course.
terra: Night glorification and praise after prostration continue 50:39's sequence through the remaining positions of the day.
terra: People emerge swiftly from the split earth for the gathering, another concrete afterlife race whose finish is God's summons.
terra: فَٱلْجَـٰرِيَـٰتِ يُسْرًا depicts vessels or movers running smoothly, a Qur'anic counterpart to the source's animal with an easy, well-transferred gait.

luna: The section’s dictionary form links سَبَحَ with stars moving in their courses; this ayah commands glorification at night and at the setting of the stars (وَإِدْبَارَ ٱلنُّجُومِ), joining the praise sense to a celestial passage.
terra: ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ uses the source root in its concrete sense of drawing near, clarifying the spatial force heard inside ٱلدُّنْيَا.
terra: The distance becomes two bow-lengths or nearer, completing 53:8's act of drawing near with an explicit spatial measure.
terra: فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ repeats that both ends of the sequence belong to God.
terra: The one who turns from remembrance and wants only ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا combines abandonment of remembrance with choosing the first stage alone.
terra: People hurry toward the Caller with humbled eyes, making the resurrection's movement an urgent procession rather than the preferred near-life race.
terra: God has made the Quran easy for remembrance; the ayah closely joins divine easing to the remembering stance developed in the section.
terra: The same declaration that the Quran was made easy for remembrance recurs after a second warning, so this repeated occurrence has its own contextual force.
terra: A third narrative cycle again ends by making the Quran easy for remembrance, preserving the surah's deliberate refrain.
terra: The refrain that the Quran was made easy for remembrance returns after Lot's people, completing the repeated formulation rather than merely echoing one occurrence.

luna: The section’s claim that what lasts outlives the run is bounded by this ayah: all who are on earth pass away (كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ), while 55:27 names what remains. | terra: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ states the exhaustion of every creature on earth, the first half of the section's passing-versus-remaining relation.

luna: The section’s root ب ق ي concerns endurance; following 55:26’s passing of all on earth, this ayah says the face of the Lord remains (وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ), giving permanence a divine rather than worldly measure. | terra: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ completes 55:26 with what remains after every earthly entrant passes.

luna: The section itself cites وَٱلسَّٰبِقُونَ ٱلسَّٰبِقُونَ; this ayah turns the race’s “foremost” into a named human group, bringing the image of first position into the Qur’an’s account of the next life. | terra: وَٱلسَّـٰبِقُونَ ٱلسَّـٰبِقُونَ places the true foremost at the head of the final human ranks.
terra: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ gives the destination and rank of the forerunners named in 56:10.
terra: فِى جَنَّـٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ states where the foremost runners of 56:10-11 finish.
terra: ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ places a large company of the former peoples within the foremost rank.
terra: وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ adds the later company behind 56:13, continuing the first-and-later ordering inside the race passage.
terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ closes the surah that ranked the foremost, right, and left companies, joining the glorifying command to the race of final ranks.
terra: هُوَ ٱلْأَوَّلُ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرُ places God at both ends of the sequence, a boundary to applying the creaturely race's before-and-after to Him.

luna: The section says the first arrival in this race is not the winner; this ayah provides a boundary: those who spent and fought before the Conquest are greater in rank than those after it (أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً), so precedence matters in this distinct context. | terra: Those who spent and fought before the victory receive a greater rank than later participants, showing a case where morally costly precedence does affect final placement, though both receive good.

luna: The section turns the two lives into a race; this ayah says people compete in worldly wealth and children (وَتَفَاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ), then depicts the growth that dries and becomes debris before contrasting the Hereafter. | terra: Worldly life blooms like rain-fed growth and then becomes debris; its rapid course supplies the passing first stage from which 57:21 redirects the race.

luna: The section’s race corrects preference for the near life; this ayah commands, “Race toward forgiveness” (سَابِقُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ), and a Garden, so the race is toward the later good. | terra: سَابِقُوٓا۟ directs the race toward forgiveness and a garden, relocating competitive speed from the passing world of 57:20 to the lasting goal.
terra: ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم بِرُسُلِنَا describes messengers following one another on predecessors' tracks.

luna: The section names ء ث ر as preferring one thing ahead of another; this ayah uses that root for people who prefer others over themselves even when needy, reversing the preference for one’s own near worldly life. | terra: وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ uses the same preference root for putting others ahead of oneself, a concrete ethical reversal of preferring the near life.

luna: The section orders a procession from what comes first to what follows; this ayah tells believers to consider what each soul has sent ahead for tomorrow (مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ), turning present action toward a later reckoning. | terra: Each soul must inspect مَا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ, making present deeds provisions sent forward to tomorrow.
luna: The section’s horse line is a moving order; this ayah praises believers who fight “in ranks” (صَفًّا) like a compact wall, a disciplined human formation rather than a race.

luna: The section pairs remembrance of God with prayer and develops a racing procession; this ayah calls believers to hurry to God’s remembrance and leave trade when prayer is announced (فَٱسْعَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ), making worship the priority over immediate gain. | terra: At the call to prayer, believers must فَٱسْعَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ and leave trade; prayer, running toward remembrance, and setting aside the near gain meet in one command.

luna: Immediately after the prayer priority of 62:9, this ayah says to spread through the land and seek God’s bounty once prayer ends; it bounds the section’s preference warning by showing worldly work resuming in the proper order. | terra: After the prayer of 62:9, believers disperse, seek God's bounty, and continue remembering Him; it marks the ordered return to provision after trade was set aside.
terra: Wealth and children must not distract from ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ; the ayah states the choice between near possessions and the remembrance that precedes prayer in the section.
terra: God will make ease after hardship, explicitly arranging hardship and ease as successive stages.
terra: After the destroyed people pass, no remaining one can be seen; the negative remnant supplies a concrete boundary to the positive endurance claimed by أَبْقَىٰ.

luna: This ayah tells the people of the right to eat and drink in satisfaction for what they sent ahead in past days; it makes the section’s temporal ordering concrete as present reward for earlier action. | terra: The people of the garden are told to enjoy what they sent ahead in bygone days, showing the later benefit of capacity conserved and forwarded during the first stage.
terra: Those who pray are excepted from the anxious, hoarding human type, giving prayer a concrete contrary course.
terra: The praying group is constant in its prayer, joining ṣalāh to endurance rather than a brief early burst.
terra: People emerge from graves سِرَاعًا as if racing to a marker, an afterlife rush that reverses the assumption that the only race is in the near life.
terra: سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا is usually understood as long daytime occupation or movement; it may preserve the motion breadth of س ب ح outside literal water, though the exact image is less certain.
terra: Whatever good people تُقَدِّمُوا۟ for themselves will be found with God خَيْرًا, making an act sent ahead become the better later possession.

luna: The section’s front/rear procession becomes an explicit choice here: whoever wills may “advance or lag behind” (يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ), so position in the course marks a moral response. | terra: The warning addresses whoever chooses أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ, turning moral response into advancing or falling behind.
terra: A person is told بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ, turning deeds into things placed ahead and left behind before the same surah contrasts immediate and later life.

luna: The section’s wording compares preferring the near life with a race’s first arrival; this ayah names what people love as the “immediate” (ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ), making the pull of what arrives first explicit. | terra: تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ names love of what arrives quickly, the closest parallel to preferring the near life and mistaking the first arrival for the better goal.

luna: The section’s wording says the later life is better and longer-lasting; this ayah supplies the other half of its near/later contrast: people leave “the Hereafter” (ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ) behind. | terra: وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ completes 75:20: the later thing is left behind while the immediately arriving thing is loved.

luna: Where the section criticizes choosing one’s immediate life first, this ayah depicts people feeding the poor, orphan, and captive despite their love of the food (عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ), a specific reversal of self-prioritizing desire.
terra: Remembering the Lord morning and evening lays remembrance across the daily sequence immediately before 76:27 condemns love of the immediate life.
terra: Night prostration and long glorification continue the ordered worship of 76:25 before the contrast with the immediately arriving life.

luna: The section’s words place the immediate life first and the Hereafter later; this ayah says people love the immediate (يُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ) and leave a weighty Day behind them, a particularly close formulation of the section’s misordered race. | terra: People love ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ and leave وَرَآءَهُمْ a heavy day; the ayah turns temporal priority into the section's literal front-and-behind arrangement.

luna: The section explicitly cites وَٱلسَّٰبِحَٰتِ سَبْحًا: Qur’an’s oath uses the same س ب ح root for runners/swimmers, giving its horse procession a direct Qur’anic counterpart. | terra: وَٱلسَّـٰبِحَـٰتِ سَبْحًا is the Qur'anic oath explicitly activated by the source section's running/swimming sense of س ب ح.

luna: The section’s dictionary phrase السَّابِقُ الأَوَّل places a horse first; this ayah names those “outstripping in a race” (فَٱلسَّٰبِقَٰتِ سَبْقًا), continuing 79:3’s runners and making the lead position explicit. | terra: فَٱلسَّـٰبِقَـٰتِ سَبْقًا immediately turns the swimmers of 79:3 into forerunners, making their motion a race with ordered positions.
terra: Pharaoh's أَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ places a false claimant to “the highest” in the same surah as the swimmers and the preference for the near life.
terra: نَكَالَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ places latter and former in one compact sequence inside the same surah as the swimmers and worldly preference.

luna: This ayah identifies the one who transgressed; 79:38 states the specific choice as preferring worldly life, so its own contribution is to frame that preference as the first of two opposed courses. | terra: فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ opens the case whose defining choice is worldly preference in 79:38.

luna: The section explicitly recalls this surah’s wording وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا: its named ء ث ر preference root and the near life occur together in the person who chooses the first life. | terra: وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا repeats the section's decisive act: putting the nearer life first.

luna: After the worldly-life preference named in 79:38, this ayah gives the transgressor’s destination as Hell (ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ), reversing the assumption that the first life’s choice secures the win. | terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ supplies the finish reached by the worldly preference of 79:38.

luna: The section says the one behind is better and lasts longer; this ayah sets against worldly desire the person who fears standing before the Lord and restrains the self from desire, the opposite ordering of what to pursue. | terra: The opposing runner fears standing before his Lord and restrains desire, answering the preference described in 79:38.

luna: This ayah names the Garden as the abode (فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ), giving the section’s later life a concrete destination after 79:40’s restraint. | terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ supplies the other finish and completes the paired routes of 79:37-40.

luna: The section says the later life outlasts the near one; this ayah says that on seeing the Hour people will feel they had stayed only an evening or its morning (عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا), sharply shrinking the worldly interval.
terra: Each soul learns مَا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ, the same front-and-back ordering applied to its own record.

luna: The section makes a race out of choosing between lives; this ayah says of the sealed drink of the righteous, “for that let competitors compete” (فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ ٱلْمُتَنَٰفِسُونَ), redirecting competition toward the lasting reward. | terra: فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ ٱلْمُتَنَـٰفِسُونَ commands competition for the sealed drink of the blessed, identifying the lasting prize for which the race should be run.
terra: لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍ may picture passage from stage to stage, a plausible ordered-course parallel, but it does not specify racers or their relative rank.
terra: يَـٰلَيْتَنِى قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِى is the late realization that one should have sent something ahead for the life that truly counts.
terra: وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَىٰهَا makes the moon follow the sun, a celestial version of the second runner immediately following the leader.

luna: The section presents life as a race with differently valued destinations; this ayah says human striving takes divergent courses (إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ), making the difference of direction explicit.

luna: The section’s dictionary form of ي س ر describes an animal’s easy transfer of its legs; this ayah says God eases the giver and God-fearer toward ease (فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ), while 92:5–6 identify that course’s choice. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ closely repeats the promise of being eased toward the easy course, now as the outcome of giving, fear, and truthfulness.

luna: The section’s dictionary form of ي س ر evokes easy movement; this paired ayah says the denier is eased toward hardship (فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ), the opposite course to the ease of 92:7. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ uses the same movement toward an end for the opposite course, showing that ease of progress does not by itself identify the good destination.
terra: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلْـَٔاخِرَةَ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ gathers the latter and former stages under God's ownership rather than the runner's preference.
terra: وَلَلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ states in one line that what comes later is better than what comes first.
terra: The promise that ease is with hardship gives a direct repeated formulation of divine ease without turning it into mere speed.
terra: The immediate repetition that ease is with hardship reinforces 94:5 as a sustained promise rather than a passing first appearance.

luna: The section’s running-horse image has a direct counterpart in the chargers “panting as they gallop” (وَٱلْعَادِيَٰتِ ضَبْحًا); this is a charge rather than a race, but supplies the same bodily motion. | terra: وَٱلْعَـٰدِيَـٰتِ ضَبْحًا stages actual galloping, panting horses, the clearest Qur'anic realization of the section's running train.

luna: The section’s running-horse scene continues here with sparks struck by the chargers’ hooves (فَٱلْمُورِيَٰتِ قَدْحًا); 100:1 identifies the galloping animals, while this ayah adds their forceful contact with the ground. | terra: The galloping animals strike sparks, continuing the bodily speed introduced in 100:1.

luna: Following the chargers named in 100:1, this ayah adds their dawn raid (فَٱلْمُغِيرَٰتِ صُبْحًا); the racing body becomes a moving group with a destination. | terra: The runners raid at dawn, fixing the horse train's movement in a temporal sequence.

luna: The chargers’ sequence continues from 100:1; this ayah’s own action is raising a cloud of dust (فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِۦ نَقْعًا), making their passage visible. | terra: The horses raise a cloud of dust, showing the shared track and force of the moving company.

luna: After the gallopers of 100:1 and the dust of 100:4, this ayah says they penetrate into the midst of a gathering (فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِۦ جَمْعًا), completing the charge’s forward movement. | terra: They penetrate the center of a gathered host, giving the running line an attained endpoint.

luna: The section’s race exposes misdirected preference; this ayah says rivalry for increase distracts people (أَلْهَىٰكُمُ ٱلتَّكَاثُرُ), naming a worldly contest that does not secure the later prize.

luna: This ayah says that rivalry continues until people visit the graves (حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ); it gives 102:1’s contest its stopping point and a boundary against mistaking duration in the world for lasting success.
